gui.siegeworks.manual.wiki: Read more on the Siegeworks wiki
gui.siegeworks.manual.build.quality: Material cost depends on blueprint quality.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ink.1: Ink is used both to make the drawing table and to trace blueprints. Two blocks are needed to begin.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ink.2: A copper inkwell becomes an ink block when combined with an ink sac, coal or charcoal.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ink.3: The ingredients can be arranged in any order. Both ink recipes are shown on the facing page.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tools.1: The drawing table provides blueprints for siege engines and handheld firearms. Any planks and logs work in its recipe.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tools.2: Paper and an ink block occupy the table slots. The selected design determines the blueprint being drawn.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tools.3: The construction hammer is used at the building site: it places projects, joins their parts and opens maintenance.
gui.siegeworks.manual.draw.1: A blueprint specifies a machine and its materials. Designs on the drawing table are completed by tracing their outlines.
gui.siegeworks.manual.draw.2: Holding the left mouse button fills the lines along the contour. Paper and ink must be in the table slots.
gui.siegeworks.manual.draw.3: Tracing accuracy determines blueprint quality. A careful drawing reduces the materials needed for construction.
gui.siegeworks.manual.parts.1: Engines combine ordinary resources with prepared components. Wheels are shared by several types of mobile equipment.
gui.siegeworks.manual.parts.2: A wheel recipe produces two wheels. An iron barrel is made one at a time.
gui.siegeworks.manual.parts.3: The selected blueprint lists the components and quantities for that engine, taking drawing quality into account.
gui.siegeworks.manual.build.1: Placing a blueprint creates an unfinished engine. The hammer goes in the main hand, the blueprint in the offhand; %1$s confirms the position.
gui.siegeworks.manual.build.2: Construction proceeds part by part. The highlighted section identifies the current stage and its materials.
gui.siegeworks.manual.build.3: Using the hammer with %1$s takes resources from inventory. Completing a stage opens the next section.
gui.siegeworks.manual.placement.1: The placement ghost shows where the finished engine will stand. Its body and moving parts need sufficient clearance.
gui.siegeworks.manual.placement.2: A project can rest on blocks or a solid structure surface using Axiomata collision geometry.
gui.siegeworks.manual.placement.3: A moving support carries the unfinished project and the completed engine with it.
gui.siegeworks.manual.controls.1: An operating position connects the player to the engine. %1$s with an empty hand mounts it; movement keys drive mobile machines.
gui.siegeworks.manual.controls.2: Camera movement controls the aim. %4$s allows a free look without changing the weapon direction.
gui.siegeworks.manual.controls.3: Field guns also offer a barrel view through %5$s. Each engine has its own aiming limits.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tower_crossbow.1: The tower crossbow is a stationary weapon with full horizontal traverse. Its ammunition is the long siege bolt.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tower_crossbow.2: Inserting a bolt starts winding. The operator mounts empty-handed, aims with the camera and fires with %2$s.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tower_crossbow.3: Tension sets the range. Once wound, it can be adjusted empty-handed with %3$s + %1$s.
gui.siegeworks.manual.arcballista.1: The arcballista combines a heavy crossbow with a wheeled carriage. It uses short siege bolts.
gui.siegeworks.manual.arcballista.2: Loading starts winding. The operator turns the chassis with movement keys, adjusts elevation with the camera and fires with %2$s.
gui.siegeworks.manual.arcballista.3: Tension is adjusted empty-handed through %3$s + %1$s. Draft towing is described in the operation chapter.
gui.siegeworks.manual.culverin.1: The culverin is a wheeled field gun. A shot needs %6$s measures of powder and %7$s mm round shot; grapeshot can replace the ball.
gui.siegeworks.manual.culverin.2: Loading has four actions: pouring powder, ramming, inserting the projectile and ramming again.
gui.siegeworks.manual.culverin.3: Each action finishes by holding %1$s to the end of its bar. The operator ignites the loaded gun with flint and steel.
gui.siegeworks.manual.serpentine.1: The serpentine is a field gun with a larger powder charge: %6$s measures, with %7$s mm round shot or grapeshot.
gui.siegeworks.manual.serpentine.2: Powder is rammed first, then the projectile is inserted and rammed. An action is unfinished while its bar is still filling.
gui.siegeworks.manual.serpentine.3: The operator aims and ignites the loaded gun with flint and steel. A draft mount can transport the carriage.
gui.siegeworks.manual.mons_meg.1: Mons Meg is a heavy bombard firing %7$s mm stone shot. Its charge requires %6$s measures of black powder.
gui.siegeworks.manual.mons_meg.2: Powder and projectile are rammed separately. Both ramrod stages must finish before ignition.
gui.siegeworks.manual.mons_meg.3: The operator aims and ignites the gun with flint and steel. Grapeshot can replace the giant stone ball.
gui.siegeworks.manual.onager.1: The onager is a mobile stone thrower. It accepts stones, stone grapeshot and prepared incendiary pots.
gui.siegeworks.manual.onager.2: Inserting ammunition starts winding. Once it finishes, %2$s fires from the operator position; empty-handed %1$s can also release the mechanism.
gui.siegeworks.manual.onager.3: Tension affects throwing range. Once wound, it can be adjusted empty-handed with %3$s + %1$s.
gui.siegeworks.manual.trebuchet.1: The trebuchet is a large stationary stone thrower. Before loading, empty-handed %1$s turns the engine towards the player.
gui.siegeworks.manual.trebuchet.2: Its ammunition includes stones, stone grapeshot and pots. The winding mechanism must finish after loading.
gui.siegeworks.manual.trebuchet.3: %3$s + %1$s adjusts tension. Empty-handed %1$s releases the wound mechanism.
gui.siegeworks.manual.hwacha.1: The hwacha fires volleys of Singijeons. Standard and explosive rockets can share the same loading.
gui.siegeworks.manual.hwacha.2: Rockets can be inserted individually or in a batch. The operator sets the direction and ignites the volley with flint and steel.
gui.siegeworks.manual.hwacha.3: Empty-handed %3$s + %1$s removes unwanted rockets. The ammunition mix determines the effects of the volley.
gui.siegeworks.manual.supplies.1: Black powder supplies cannons, the hand cannon and arquebus. Its recipe combines gunpowder with two charcoal.
gui.siegeworks.manual.supplies.2: The large ramrod serves cannons. Handheld firearms use a separate small ramrod; the tools are not interchangeable.
gui.siegeworks.manual.supplies.3: During loading, the progress bar represents the action duration. Its ingredient is held until the bar fills.
gui.siegeworks.manual.casting.1: The casting table produces iron ammunition in the required caliber. It accepts iron ingots.
gui.siegeworks.manual.casting.2: The − and + buttons choose the size. Weapon and ammunition tooltips specify the required caliber.
gui.siegeworks.manual.casting.3: The table previews iron cost and batch output. Finished rounds are delivered to inventory.
gui.siegeworks.manual.stone_shot.1: Stone shot is worked in a stonecutter. It needs no iron and is not made on the casting table.
gui.siegeworks.manual.stone_shot.2: Regular 120 mm stone shot fits field guns. Giant 490 mm shot is intended for Mons Meg.
gui.siegeworks.manual.stone_shot.3: One stone block yields four regular balls or one giant ball. Material affects projectile mass and penetration.
gui.siegeworks.manual.bolts.1: Siege crossbows use different ammunition: long bolts for the tower crossbow, short bolts for the arcballista.
gui.siegeworks.manual.bolts.2: Inserting a suitable bolt starts winding. An engine will not accept incompatible ammunition.
gui.siegeworks.manual.bolts.3: Tension affects range. A bolt can pass through an entity and continue flying if it has enough energy to penetrate.
gui.siegeworks.manual.grapeshot.1: Grapeshot spreads into multiple damaging elements, making it useful against groups of targets.
gui.siegeworks.manual.grapeshot.2: For cannons it replaces the round shot in the loading sequence. Powder and ramrod stages are still required.
gui.siegeworks.manual.grapeshot.3: Stone grapeshot for the onager and trebuchet is a separate ammunition item. Its recipe is shown opposite.
gui.siegeworks.manual.rockets.1: Small Singijeons damage by direct impact. Large Singijeons carry an explosive charge and can cause fires.
gui.siegeworks.manual.rockets.2: Both types are used by the hwacha. A mixed loading combines their effects in one volley.
gui.siegeworks.manual.rockets.3: Rockets can be loaded separately or in batches. The ammunition mix can still be changed before ignition.
gui.siegeworks.manual.pot.1: A clay pot holds an incendiary mixture. An empty shell must first be placed to receive its contents.
gui.siegeworks.manual.pot.2: The base and additives determine the charge properties. String seals the filled pot.
gui.siegeworks.manual.pot.3: Flint and steel lights the fuse. The pot bursts on impact or when its fuse burns out, so ignition belongs just before use.
gui.siegeworks.manual.pot_filling.1: The base consists of one charcoal and one honeycomb. Additional ingredients change the charge properties.
gui.siegeworks.manual.pot_filling.2: Up to six additives fit inside, with a maximum of three of one kind. Their effects are listed opposite.
gui.siegeworks.manual.pot_filling.3: String seals the shell. The finished pot tooltip lists its contents; flint and steel ignites it before firing.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ballistics.1: Speed, material and obstacles affect penetration and direct damage. Cover changes the outcome of an impact.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ballistics.2: Destroyed blocks produce dangerous debris. A nearby target can be hit even if the projectile itself missed it.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ballistics.3: Fire arrows ignite when the shooter has flint and steel. Their recipe is shown opposite.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ladder_craft.1: A siege ladder is assembled in sections. The first recipe makes a base from logs and sticks.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ladder_craft.2: To extend it, the same recipe replaces the bottom middle stick with an existing siege ladder.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ladder_craft.3: The maximum is four sections. Their count appears in the item tooltip, so length can be checked before placement.
gui.siegeworks.manual.siege_ladder.1: A siege ladder creates a route over a tall obstacle. Placement through %1$s aligns its incline with a support.
gui.siegeworks.manual.siege_ladder.2: Empty-handed %3$s + %1$s picks it up. Repeating the action places the ladder again.
gui.siegeworks.manual.siege_ladder.3: Carrying occupies both hands. The ladder length depends on the sections added during crafting.
gui.siegeworks.manual.forked_pole.1: The forked pole is a long-reaching weapon and a wall defence tool. It can push an attacking siege ladder away.
gui.siegeworks.manual.forked_pole.2: Bracing takes place from the wall side near the upper end of the ladder, while aiming the pole and holding %1$s.
gui.siegeworks.manual.forked_pole.3: A brief shove may be insufficient. Releasing the brace before completion can allow the ladder to return.
gui.siegeworks.manual.battering_ram.1: The battering ram delivers heavy blows to fortifications. Its head transmits an impact into neighbouring connected blocks.
gui.siegeworks.manual.battering_ram.2: Crew members occupy the pushing positions to move it. A second pusher helps transport the machine.
gui.siegeworks.manual.battering_ram.3: An empty-handed %3$s + %1$s delivers a manual strike when all crew positions are vacant.
gui.siegeworks.manual.mantlet.1: The mantlet is a movable cover with a shutter. Its body protects those behind it and loses durability under impact.
gui.siegeworks.manual.mantlet.2: The operating position controls the shutter: %2$s raises it and %3$s lowers it.
gui.siegeworks.manual.mantlet.3: Mounting requires an empty hand. Pressing %3$s twice leaves the position behind the shield.
gui.siegeworks.manual.siege_tower.1: The siege tower carries troops towards fortifications. Internal ladders (1) connect its floors; holding %2$s climbs them.
gui.siegeworks.manual.siege_tower.2: The top-floor mechanism (2) controls the drawbridge through empty-handed %1$s.
gui.siegeworks.manual.siege_tower.3: %3$s + %1$s adjusts the landing angle. The illustration shows the bridge lowered and the lower section covered with leather.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tower_crew.1: Moving a tower needs the rear driver and at least one pusher. Additional crew occupy the other positions.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tower_crew.2: Leather covering increases durability and fire protection. Each layer takes 64 leather, with the lower section covered first.
gui.siegeworks.manual.tower_crew.3: Shears with %3$s remove the covering, allowing protection to be changed after construction.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_craft.1: The hand cannon and arquebus use blueprints from the same drawing table. They are assembled directly as items.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_craft.2: Using a blueprint opens its assembly screen. Materials are checked in inventory and the manufacture button delivers the result.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_craft.3: Each assembly consumes one blueprint. The facing page lists materials for both firearms.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_tools.1: The firearm lock is a component of the arquebus. The hand cannon needs no separate lock: its charge is ignited externally.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_tools.2: The small ramrod serves both handheld firearms. The cannon ramrod is not a substitute.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_tools.3: Ramming spends the small ramrod durability. This wearing tool is required to prepare another charge.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_load.1: Handheld firearms are loaded from the offhand. The sequence is black powder, a suitable ball and the small ramrod.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_load.2: Each action continues while %1$s is held. A filled bar marks its completion.
gui.siegeworks.manual.firearm_load.3: The required item can be fed temporarily from the hotbar. The previous offhand item is returned after the action.
gui.siegeworks.manual.hand_cannon.1: The hand cannon uses %7$s mm iron balls and external ignition. Powder and ball are seated with the small ramrod.
gui.siegeworks.manual.hand_cannon.2: Holding %1$s aims the weapon. %2$s with flint and steel in the offhand or hotbar ignites the priming.
gui.siegeworks.manual.hand_cannon.3: The priming burns briefly before the shot. Ignition and the ball leaving the barrel are separated by a noticeable delay.
gui.siegeworks.manual.arquebus.1: The arquebus uses %7$s mm iron balls. Loading follows the hand cannon, but its own matchlock performs ignition.
gui.siegeworks.manual.arquebus.2: String serves as the match. Once fitted and lit with flint and steel, it remains ready for the trigger.
gui.siegeworks.manual.arquebus.3: With a burning match, %1$s aims and %2$s releases the shot immediately, without a new ignition wait.
gui.siegeworks.manual.match.1: One string serves an arquebus for %8$s shots. A lit match stays ready between them.
gui.siegeworks.manual.match.2: Water extinguishes the flame. Empty offhand and %3$s + %1$s also put it out manually.
gui.siegeworks.manual.match.3: Firearms gradually wear out. Iron repairs their durability on an anvil.
gui.siegeworks.manual.towing.1: A draft harness transports compatible wheeled engines from a mount. The animal must be tamed, with a saddle where applicable.
gui.siegeworks.manual.towing.2: A lead is used on the machine while the leashed animal is nearby. The rider then controls the transport.
gui.siegeworks.manual.towing.3: A lead detaches the animal. Shears remove the attachment and return the lead as an item.
gui.siegeworks.manual.maintenance.1: Completed machines can be repaired and dismantled. A construction hammer opens their maintenance screen.
gui.siegeworks.manual.maintenance.2: The screen lists repair materials, which must be in the working player's inventory.
gui.siegeworks.manual.maintenance.3: Dismantling also uses the hammer after selecting its mode. All crew positions must be vacant first.
gui.siegeworks.manual.weather.1: Engines exposed to the weather turn grey and lose durability. Rain accelerates this wear.
gui.siegeworks.manual.weather.2: Repair restores a weathered engine. A protective treatment does not replace repairing existing damage.
gui.siegeworks.manual.weather.3: Honeycomb protects supported machines from weathering. It is best applied to a repaired structure.
gui.siegeworks.manual.customization.1: The siege tower and trebuchet counterweight provide banner positions. Additional banners fill them in sequence.
gui.siegeworks.manual.customization.2: Shears remove the last fitted banner, allowing colours to change without dismantling the machine.
gui.siegeworks.manual.customization.3: Copper gives culverin and serpentine barrels a bronze appearance. This finish is decorative and does not change weapon statistics.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ownership.1: A machine belongs to the player who placed it. Their team and allied Recruits factions receive access.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ownership.2: The same access rules apply to loading, towing and maintenance. An enemy side must first capture the engine.
gui.siegeworks.manual.ownership.3: Uncrewed enemy equipment can be captured under the separate rules described on the next spread.
gui.siegeworks.manual.capture.1: Capturing changes ownership of an unattended enemy engine. It starts by taking its operating position empty-handed with no crew present.
gui.siegeworks.manual.capture.2: The bar shows capture progress. Leaving the position or taking damage interferes with completion.
gui.siegeworks.manual.capture.3: The owner side must be online. Siege ladders are excluded and cannot be captured.
gui.siegeworks.manual.recruits.1: With Recruits installed, crews are assigned through the siege category of its regular command menu.
gui.siegeworks.manual.recruits.2: Orders apply to selected squads and a machine type. This is where crew work and weapon targets are assigned.
gui.siegeworks.manual.recruits.3: An engineer can also construct engines. For this order, the commander carries the blueprint in the offhand.
gui.siegeworks.manual.supply.1: An engineer first spends materials from personal inventory. A supply container supports extended operation and repairs.
gui.siegeworks.manual.supply.2: The assigned container must hold supplies and remain within 16 blocks.
gui.siegeworks.manual.supply.3: RTS Command adds tactical-map orders and fire zones. The normal Recruits menu remains available without it.
gui.siegeworks.manual.compat.1: The forked pole uses Better Combat and Epic Fight moves when the corresponding mod is installed.
gui.siegeworks.manual.compat.2: The hand cannon and arquebus retain their loading stages and aiming in supported combat modes.
gui.siegeworks.manual.compat.3: Key names in this book follow the current control settings. Rebinding a key updates the instructions.

gui.siegeworks.recruits.siege_commands.t: Order selected groups to crew the targeted siege engine.
Assign one selected siege engineer to control the tower and order the other selected recruits inside.
Assign selected regular recruits to the tower's available pushing positions.
Order selected siege engineers to leave the engines they operate; tower passengers stay aboard.
Order selected groups to return to their assigned siege engines.
Order selected siege crews to attack the targeted position.
Stop attacking and hold the selected siege engines at their current position.
Allow selected siege crews to engage targets automatically.
Allow selected rams to charge targets on their own.
Keep bridges lowered while stationary; they close during movement.
Let siege tower crews manage bridges automatically.
Lower the bridge and safely unload owned recruits from towers controlled by the selected groups.
Bring owned recruits of the selected groups back into their towers over the bridge.
Use the first compatible ammunition available.
Use stones or solid cannon balls only.
Use the targeted container as the ammunition and construction supply point for selected siege engineers.
Order one selected siege engineer to build the offhand Siegeworks blueprint at the targeted position.
Assign one selected siege engineer to repair the targeted engine using their inventory or supply point.
Assign one selected siege engineer to dismantle the empty targeted engine.
Cancel construction, maintenance, or ladder relocation assigned to selected recruits.
Order the nearest selected free recruit to pack the targeted empty ladder into their inventory.
Place a carried ladder on top of the selected ground block, facing away from you.
